title: Migrate a parameter-grid evaluator off deprecated purrr cross() and invoke_map()
source_relation: adapted: package migration preserving behavioural semantics, expressed as a repair of a delivered function with a named-argument call contract
difficulty_hypothesis: purrr::cross() and invoke_map() were deprecated in purrr 1.0.0 and warn in the pinned version; their replacements (tidyr::expand_grid(), exec()/pmap) differ in row order and argument matching. expand.grid() makes factors by default, and positional calls break when the formals are in a different order.

mcp_relevance.rationale: Which purrr functions are deprecated, and what replaces them with what semantics, is package-version knowledge that pre-1.0 training data contradicts. The deprecation warnings themselves name the replacements, and base R expand.grid()/do.call() is a complete fallback.
mcp_relevance.information_need: Deprecation status of purrr::cross()/invoke_map() in the pinned purrr and the semantics of the replacements.
mcp_relevance.obtainable_without_mcp: partly: the warnings name tidyr::expand_grid() and exec(); base R is sufficient

pinned_evidence.observed: cross() warns 'deprecated in purrr 1.0.0, use tidyr::expand_grid()'; invoke_map() warns 'use map() + exec()'
pinned_evidence.oracle: explicit mixed-radix index arithmetic, independent of expand.grid()
